page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and includes an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on external Premium Storage options.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 105,569.39 and a multi-core stress-ng performance score of 94,844.99, placing it in the top tiers of raw compute capacity. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 345.73 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 135.88 GB/sec for write operations. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also demonstrate high throughput, with bzip3 decompression reaching 556.8 GB/sec. For database and web serving workloads, the server processed 152.07 million Redis SET operations per second and achieved a static web serving throughput of 124.31 GB/sec.

The D96s_v7 offers high resource density and compute performance, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for large-scale enterprise workloads that require massive parallel processing without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. However, the lack of local storage means all storage operations must go over the network to external Premium Storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs compared to instances with local NVMe drives. The instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference, as demonstrated by its strong prompt processing speeds across various model sizes.
